newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr but off day's low.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr but off day's low.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.89/91 per dollar, down from the opening quotes of 35.83/85 on heavy demand for the US currency, dealers said.
They said the rupee was mainly pushed down by dollar demand from a large state-run bank based in eastern India.

"Basically, it (the state-run bank) set the tone," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There were other banks in the market also, indicating both corporate demand and squaring off of short dollar positions. It all combined to drag the rupee down."
A dealer said there was also good demand for dollars from a state-run firm based in north India.
Dealers said the rupee touched a low of 35.92 before rallying on some inflows. Some dealers said the dollar inflows were from a large power company but they had no details.
"There still seems to be some unsatisfied demand," said a dealer. "If this continues and supplies do not come into the market, the 36 rupee per dollar mark will be breached soon."
Dealers said premia on forward dollars moved up on paying pressure from some importers.
They said the fall in the value of the rupee in the spot market could have led to some importers deciding to cover their positions which led to the pressure on forward premia.
"Forward premia would have moved up further but for Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention," said a dealer.
He said the RBI continued to roll over December maturity swaps, receiving premia. The RBI has been rolling over swaps since last week, he said.
The premia on six-month forward dollars ended Thursday at an annualised 7.52 percent against Wednesday's closing 7.08 percent, he said.
